correctness.rationale: Reconstructed graph adjacency and full 1009 nonempty faces; five exhaustive discrete-Morse matchings, with reversed matched edges and every other Hasse incidence oriented downward, are acyclic by complete topological sorts over 3558, 2844, 512, 2722, and 608 incidences. Their only critical cells are (one 0-cell, 22 3-cells), (one 0-cell, 14 3-cells), (one 0-cell, 8 2-cells), (one 0-cell, 20 3-cells), and (one 0-cell, 2 2-cells). Thus each integral CW homotopy model is a sphere wedge. The S4 action is transitive within exactly the triangular and reversal edge classes. Each link inclusion from a wedge of 2-spheres to a wedge of 3-spheres is nullhomotopic since pi_2 of the target vanishes, so both deletion/link cofibrations split. Independent line-graph enumeration and mod-two boundary ranks reproduce all Betti numbers; they are corroboration rather than the integral proof.

value.rationale: The truncated tetrahedron is a natural Archimedean 3-connected planar but nonouterplanar graph. Its matching-complex integral homotopy and both complete edge-orbit deletion/link types are intrinsic exact invariants; the four local sphere multiplicities and their two nullhomotopic splittings are not implied by published general estimates, nor a trivial numerical substitution. The result gives a concrete motivated polyhedral benchmark for the outerplanar-to-planar matching-complex wedge question and can be used as a local-to-global test case, without asserting any infinite-family theorem.
